Rioja.climate: Continental, tempered by the Atlantic via the Ebro valley
Rioja.agingRules: Crianza: 2yr total, min 1 in oak. Reserva: 3yr, min 1 in oak. Gran Reserva: 5yr, min 2 in oak.

Ribera del Duero.climate: High-altitude continental — big diurnal swings concentrate skins
Ribera del Duero.agingRules: Same Crianza/Reserva/Gran Reserva ladder as Rioja

Burgundy.classification: AOC, with Grand Cru/Premier Cru/Village/Regional tiers
Burgundy.climate: Cool continental — vintage variation is large and prices track it
Burgundy.agingRules: No fixed cellar mandate; single-vineyard Grand Cru sits atop a strict site-based hierarchy, not a time-in-barrel rule

Bordeaux.classification: AOC, Left Bank vs Right Bank, 1855 Classification for Médoc
Bordeaux.climate: Maritime, moderated by the Gironde estuary
Bordeaux.agingRules: Blends vary by bank: Left Bank (gravel, Médoc) leans Cabernet-dominant; Right Bank (clay, Pomerol/St-Émilion) leans Merlot-dominant

Napa Valley.climate: Warm days, fog-cooled nights off San Pablo Bay
Napa Valley.agingRules: No formal aging mandate — house style sets it, often riper and more oak-forward than Bordeaux

Piedmont.climate: Foggy, cool continental in the Langhe hills
Piedmont.agingRules: Barolo: min 38 months aging, 18 in wood. Barbaresco: min 26 months, 9 in wood.

Marlborough.climate: Sunny days, cold nights, maritime — locks in high acidity and pyrazine aromatics
Marlborough.agingRules: Not aging-focused — drunk young for freshness

Champagne.climate: Marginal cool climate — grapes barely ripen, which is what makes the base wine right for sparkling
Champagne.agingRules: Non-vintage: min 15 months on lees (12 by law, house minimums run higher). Vintage: min 3 years.

Loire Valley.agingRules: No aging mandate; Sancerre is a flint-and-citrus style meant young

Provence.agingRules: No aging mandate — pale, dry rosé built for immediate drinking

Tempranillo.profile: Medium-high tannin, red cherry and plum, leather and tobacco with bottle age

Cabernet Sauvignon.profile: High tannin, high acid, blackcurrant and cedar; thick skin gives deep color and structure

Pinot Noir.profile: Light body, high acid, low tannin; red cherry and forest floor, thin-skinned and site-transparent

Chardonnay.profile: Neutral grape that takes on winemaking choices readily — oak gives vanilla/butter, steel keeps it lean and citrus

Sauvignon Blanc.profile: High acid, herbaceous, gooseberry and passionfruit; pyrazines drive the grassy, cut-grass note

Nebbiolo.profile: High tannin AND high acid, pale color despite intensity; tar and rose petal aromatics, needs years to soften

Grenache.profile: Low tannin, high alcohol, red berry and white pepper; base grape of most dry Provençal rosé

Syrah.profile: Deep color, medium-high tannin, black pepper and blackberry, smoky at altitude

Riesling.profile: High acid, aromatic, can be bone-dry to very sweet; ages into petrol/TDN character that's a feature, not a fault

Merlot.profile: Softer tannin than Cabernet, plum and cocoa, ripens earlier; the backbone of Right Bank Bordeaux

vanilla.cause: Lactones from oak barrel aging, concentrated in American oak

coconut.cause: Same oak-lactone family as vanilla — a signature of American oak specifically

butter.cause: Diacetyl, a byproduct of malolactic fermentation converting malic acid to lactic acid

petrol.cause: TDN (a naphthalene compound) forming as Riesling ages — a hallmark of mature examples, not a flaw

smoke.cause: Guaiacol and related phenols from toasted oak, or naturally in grapes grown in volcanic/mineral soils

leather.cause: Tertiary aromas from prolonged bottle age and slow oxidation, common in aged Tempranillo and Nebbiolo

green pepper.cause: Pyrazines, most concentrated in Cabernet Franc, Sauvignon Blanc, and under-ripe Cabernet Sauvignon

tropical fruit.cause: Thiols released during fermentation, especially pronounced in warm-climate Sauvignon Blanc and Chenin Blanc

honey.cause: Botrytis (noble rot) concentrating sugars, or simple bottle-age oxidation in aromatic whites

brioche.cause: Autolysis — dead yeast cells breaking down during extended lees aging, classic in traditional-method sparkling
